pending.body: All five fixture functions (breeding_success_state, thermal_scenario_state, chemistry_stress_state, chloride_test_base_state, crash_mode_state) manually override DIC, alkalinity, and bicarbonate_mg_total after calling WaterState::default_for_volume_l, but never re-solve carbonate equilibrium before calling reseed_stability_tracker(). This leaves state.water.ph stale (derived from the default DIC=20/alk=1.5 chemistry, roughly pH 7.3) while the actual overridden chemistry (e.g., DIC=5/alk=12 in breeding_success_state) would resolve to a significantly different pH (likely >8.5). On the first hourly tick, apply_hourly_chemistry_terms calls resolve_carbonate_state, correcting pH — but the stability tracker's prev_ph still holds the stale value, causing a false instability signal from the pH discontinuity. Fix: insert a resolve_carbonate_state(&mut state.water, vol) call after setting custom DIC/alkalinity/bicarbonate and before reseed_stability_tracker() in each fixture function. This ensures the initial state is internally consistent and the stability tracker baseline matches the actual chemistry.
